data.notes:
PHOTO PORTRAIT
The head of Michelangelo's David (1501-04) etched into a flat board with a V-bit, 93 x 140 mm, in the manner of Photo V-Carve: parallel lines that are wider and deeper where the picture is darker, so the eye sees the shading of the marble.

The picture is a detail of a photograph of the statue by Jörg Bittner Unna (Wikimedia Commons), brought in with File > Import picture, V-carve as photo. Its dark background was made light first, so that only the statue is etched, and Midtones was set to 0.5 to keep the stone light. Pictures with a clear subject and good contrast work best; a busy or dark background is etched as a dark patch.

Operation
1. Photo V-carve: the 30° engraving bit etches lines 0.8 mm apart along X, up to 1.5 mm deep where the picture is black and not at all where it is white.

Before cutting for real
- Use a pale, fine-grained wood (maple, birch or poplar): the lines show best as dark on light.
- Set X0 Y0 at the lower-left corner and Z0 on the top of the stock, and tick "Air cut" for a first run.
- Check the Estimated time: closer lines (a smaller Spacing) or a shallower Depth make a finer or a faster picture.
